entry.title: Stride CLI 1.0.4
entry.content:
What's Changed

Auto-generated; a maintainer may hand-edit.

🌙 Nightly builds

  • New --nightly option for stride sdk available, stride sdk install, stride sdk update and stride upgrade. Nightly builds are now only picked when you pass --nightly, even if you also pass --prerelease.
    stride sdk install --nightly and stride sdk update --nightly add the nightly feed to your NuGet.config, the same way the launcher's "Show nightly builds" setting does, so Game Studio and your projects can restore from it later. stride sdk available --nightly only lists the nightlies and leaves your NuGet.config alone. stride sdk update also no longer moves a version line back to an older version when you're already on a newer nightly or prerelease (@xen2,

entry.title: Stride 4.4.0
entry.content:
Stride 4.4 is one of the largest updates the engine has received in years, with roughly 3200 commits since the previous version!

The main focus of this release was on modernization and reach, which includes much more stable Vulkan and Direct3D 12 backends, support for non-Windows platforms no longer being experimental and an overhaul of the shader compiler.

This update also includes many exciting new features, such as a CLI tool, ability to replace read-only assets and much more.

Highlights

Here are a few of the stand-out changes:

📱 Platform support

So far, Stride has mostly been a Windows-first engine. Other platforms were supported, but creating and running games on them would often lead to many problems. This update changes that.

All platforms have been brought back into shape and the test suite for them has been expanded to make sure they won't fall behind again. Additionally, with changes to the asset compiler, building projects on Linux and macOS now works the same as it does on Windows.

entry.title: Stride Launcher 6.0.2
entry.content:
What's Changed

Auto-generated; a maintainer may hand-edit.

🚀 Launcher

  • Fixed self-updates that require a full reinstall: the new installer is now saved to disk as it downloads instead of being held entirely in memory first, so the download no longer times out or fails on slower connections (@xen2, 027d59a)

🔧 Under the hood

  • The launcher's requests for release notes, news, documentation links and the setup download now share one HTTP client and identify themselves with a Stride-Launcher/<version> tag, making it easier to tell which launcher versions are still in use (@xen2,
